record.original_question:
A nonzero real sequence Λ = {λ_k}_{k≥0} is called a λ-sequence if,
whenever a real polynomial p(x) = Σ a_k x^k is
positive for every real x, the transformed polynomial Λ[p](x) = Σ λ_k
a_k x^k is also positive for every real x.
Characterize those positive multiplier sequences {γ_k}_{k≥0} for which
the reciprocal sequence {1/γ_k}_{k≥0} is a
λ-sequence.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Call a nonzero real sequence Λ = {λ_k}_{k≥0} a λ-sequence (equivalently, a positive definite sequence) if, for every real polynomial p(x) = Σ_{k=0}^n a_k x^k satisfying p(x) > 0 for all x ∈ ℝ, the transformed polynomial Λ[p](x) := Σ_{k=0}^n λ_k a_k x^k also satisfies Λ[p](x) > 0 for all x ∈ ℝ. Recall that a positive multiplier sequence is a sequence {γ_k}_{k≥0} of positive real numbers such that the linear operator sending x^k to γ_k x^k maps every real polynomial having only real zeros to a polynomial having only real zeros. Give a complete characterization of the positive multiplier sequences {γ_k}_{k≥0} for which the reciprocal sequence {1/γ_k}_{k≥0} is a λ-sequence.
